abstract: In eukaryotes, translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) enables replication across DNA lesions, difficult DNA structures, and during replicative stress. While TLS prevents replication fork collapse, it is inherently mutagenic and requires tight regulation to prevent global mutation rates increase. Here, we show that elevated DNA polymerase pol {zeta}/Rev1 promotes spontaneous mutagenesis during replication. The five subunits of pol zeta complex (pol zeta5) are the catalytic subunit Rev3, the TLS polymerase Rev1, a dimer of accessory protein Rev7, the Pol31 and Pol32 subunits shared with replicative pol delta. Pol31 and Pol32 bind the Fe-S-containing C-terminal domain (CTD) of Rev3, which serves as a major assembly hub. We found that overproduction of pol zeta5, but not four-subunit pol zeta4 lacking Rev1 or Rev1 alone, increases spontaneous mutation rates by up to 20-fold, indicating that pol zeta5 can access undamaged DNA during replication and compete with replicative DNA polymerases. This mutator effect is independent of PCNA ubiquitylation. augments by hydroxyurea and synergizes with DNA mismatch repair defects. Overproduction of a pol zeta5 complex containing CTD-truncated Rev3 is also mutagenic, demonstrating that active TLS complexes can assemble and function without the canonical CTD interaction hub. Both complexes predominantly generate CG-to-GC transversions, a mutational pattern that resembles several COSMIC cancer mutational signatures. Inactivating Rev3 catalytic activity abolishes mutagenesis, whereas loss of Rev1 catalytic activity substantially reduces mutation rates and eliminates CG-to-GC transversions, identifying Rev1 as the primary cause of the observed mutation pattern. The findings reveal previously unrecognized mechanisms of pol zeta-dependent mutagenesis with broad implications for cellular evolution and cancer development

summary: Overproduced eukaryotic pol zeta/Rev1 (pol zeta5) raises spontaneous mutation rates up to 20-fold, generating CG-to-GC transversions via Rev1 catalysis.
title: Minimal eukaryotic DNA polymerase zeta/Rev1 GC-pair mutasome
